entries.title: Do you need to add numbers to solve Sudoku?
entries.answer: A common Sudoku puzzle has nine rows, nine columns, and nine little squares containing nine spaces each. Put the digits one through nine into the empty spaces so each digit appears once in every row, column, and little square. You do not have to do sums. Instead, look for places where some digits cannot go because they already appear nearby. Sometimes all those limits leave just one choice.
facts: You could play the same kind of puzzle with nine different symbols instead of digits.

entries.title: How do dominoes fit into a chain?
entries.answer: A domino is a tile marked into two halves. Each half can have dots or be blank. In a familiar matching game, players take turns adding a tile to an open end of the row. The number of dots on the touching ends must match. A tile showing three on each half is a double three. Other domino games use the same tiles with different rules for building or scoring.
facts: The blank end of a domino has zero dots.

entries.title: How do stones surround space in Go?
entries.answer: Go is a board game in which two players take turns putting black and white stones where lines cross. Once a stone is placed, it stays there unless it is captured. A stone or connected group needs empty points next to it, along the lines. If the other player occupies the last of those neighboring empty points, they take the group off the board. Players also use lines of their stones to surround open space.
facts: The usual full-sized Go board has nineteen lines in each direction. Beginners often use smaller boards.

entries.title: What can seven tangram pieces make?
entries.answer: A tangram is a set of seven flat pieces that can be arranged into a square. Moving the pieces apart gives you shapes to build new pictures. Many puzzles show only an outline of a bird, boat, or person. You have to fill the outline without gaps or overlapping pieces. A large triangle that looks wrong at first may fit if you turn it around or use two smaller triangles elsewhere.
facts: A traditional tangram has five triangles, one square, and one parallelogram.

entries.title: What changes when a checker becomes a king?
entries.answer: In English draughts, often called checkers, each player starts with pieces on the dark squares of a board. An ordinary piece moves one square diagonally forward to an empty space. It can capture an opposing piece by jumping diagonally forward over it to the empty square just beyond. When a piece reaches the farthest row on the other side, it becomes a king. From then on, it can move and capture diagonally forward or backward.
facts: If a capture is available in standard English draughts, the player must make a capture.

entries.title: What does checkmate mean in chess?
entries.answer: In chess, a king is in check when one of the other player’s pieces attacks the square it is on. The player has to answer the threat. They might move the king to a safe square, capture the threatening piece, or place another piece between them. When none of those choices can make the king safe, it is checkmate. The game ends before anyone actually takes the king off the board.
facts: If the player has no legal move and the king is safe from check, the game is a draw called stalemate.

entries.title: Why do jigsaws have edge pieces?
entries.answer: In a rectangular jigsaw, the pieces at the outside have at least one straight edge. That makes them easier to sort before you look for a place for each one. Pieces in the middle can give you clues by their shapes, their colors, and the parts of the picture they show. Matching a piece by color alone may fool you, so also check how well its edge fits.
facts: Some early jigsaw puzzles were made by mounting maps on boards and cutting out the areas to make pieces.

entries.title: Why do mancala games use rows of pits?
entries.answer: Mancala is a family of board games that use small pieces and rows of hollow places. In many versions you pick up all the pieces from a pit, then put them down one at a time in later pits as you go around the board. This move is sometimes called sowing. Where the last piece lands can matter a lot. It may give another turn, allow a capture, or simply end the move, depending on the rules.
facts: People can play games in this family with seeds, shells, stones, or other counters.

entries.title: Why does a chess knight move in an L?
entries.answer: The knight in chess looks like a horse’s head. Its move ends two squares away in one direction and one square to the side. That makes the shape of the letter L when you count the squares. Pieces in between do not stop the move, so a knight can move over them. It cannot end on a square with one of its own team’s pieces. Near a corner it has fewer places to go.
facts: A knight’s move always takes it from a light square to a dark one or from a dark square to a light one.
